claim: The new packaging system yields titers orders of magnitude higher than previous methods for RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c rabies viral vectors.
source: Here, we report the development of an improved packaging system for the production of the highly neurotropic RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c rabies viral vectors, yielding titers orders of magnitude higher with no background contamination, at a fraction of the production time, while preserving the efficiency of transsynaptic labeling.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that the new system yields titers orders of magnitude higher, and Figure 1H shows quantitative comparison of titers between the new and old production methods.

claim: The new packaging system produces RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c vectors with no background contamination.
source: Here, we report the development of an improved packaging system for the production of the highly neurotropic RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c rabies viral vectors, yielding titers orders of magnitude higher with no background contamination, at a fraction of the production time, while preserving the efficiency of transsynaptic labeling.
evidence: The manuscript states no background contamination is observed, and experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 demonstrates minimal non-specific labeling.

claim: The new packaging system reduces production time to a fraction of previous methods.
source: Here, we report the development of an improved packaging system for the production of the highly neurotropic RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c rabies viral vectors, yielding titers orders of magnitude higher with no background contamination, at a fraction of the production time, while preserving the efficiency of transsynaptic labeling.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 provide quantitative comparison of production timelines, showing rescue timeline reduced from 10-11 days to 5-6 days, and pseudotyping timeline reduced from 28 days to 4-6 days.

claim: The new packaging system preserves the efficiency of transsynaptic labeling of RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c vectors.
source: Here, we report the development of an improved packaging system for the production of the highly neurotropic RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c rabies viral vectors, yielding titers orders of magnitude higher with no background contamination, at a fraction of the production time, while preserving the efficiency of transsynaptic labeling.
evidence: Figure 3 shows comparative retrograde labeling efficiency experiments demonstrating that vectors produced with the new system maintain comparable efficiency to N2A-produced vectors.

claim: The new system uncovered hidden local and distal inhibitory connections in the mouse hippocampal formation.
source: We demonstrate the power and flexibility of the new system by uncovering hidden local and distal inhibitory connections in the mouse hippocampal formation and by imaging the functional properties of a cortical microcircuit across weeks.
evidence: Figure 4 shows identification of previously unreported inhibitory projections from CA1 S.O. and S.LM. to dentate gyrus, as well as excitatory projections from subiculum.

claim: The new system enables imaging of functional properties of a cortical microcircuit across weeks.
source: We demonstrate the power and flexibility of the new system by uncovering hidden local and distal inhibitory connections in the mouse hippocampal formation and by imaging the functional properties of a cortical microcircuit across weeks.
evidence: Figure 7 demonstrates in vivo two-photon calcium imaging of GCaMP8m-labeled neurons in V1 from day 3 to day 16 post-injection, showing maintained functional properties.

claim: Most tools currently used to explore connectivity have low throughput, low selectivity, or limited accessibility.
source: However, most tools currently used to explore connectivity have low throughput, low selectivity, or limited accessibility.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the field, drawing on established knowledge about existing connectivity mapping tools.

claim: Monosynaptic tracing technologies based on engineered rabies virus enable cell-type specific labeling of presynaptic partners.
source: In contrast, monosynaptic tracing technologies, based on engineered rabies virus, enable cell-type specific labeling of presynaptic partners, making it one of the most powerful toolkits to genetically dissect neuronal populations.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established rabies tracing methodology (Ginger et al., 2013; Wickersham et al., 2007a; Zampieri et al., 2014).

claim: G-deleted rabies viral vectors pseudotyped with envA propagate exclusively from TVA- and G-expressing starter cells to their presynaptic partners.
source: in the second step, G-deleted rabies viral vectors, pseudotyped with the Avian Sarcoma and Leukosis Virus's envelope glycoprotein A (envA) are introduced to the region containing TVA- and G-expressing neurons (Figure 1B), resulting in propagation of rabies particles exclusively from these starter cells to their presynaptic partners, but not to disynaptically connected neurons, and rarely to post-synaptic targets (Zampieri et al., 2014), regardless of their physical proximity (Ginger et al., 2013; Wickersham et al., 2007a; Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by citations to foundational rabies tracing papers (Ginger et al., 2013; Wickersham et al., 2007a; Zampieri et al., 2014) and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: G-deleted rabies vectors rarely propagate to post-synaptic targets.
source: resulting in propagation of rabies particles exclusively from these starter cells to their presynaptic partners, but not to disynaptically connected neurons, and rarely to post-synaptic targets (Zampieri et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zampieri et al., 2014.

claim: Inefficiencies in the SAD B19 strain and potential transmission biases across cell types suggest traced cells might represent only a fraction of the complete presynaptic population.
source: While this approach ostensibly identifies presynaptic partners associated with a predesignated starter population, inefficiencies in the widely used SAD B19 strain, along with potential transmission biases across cell types (Albisetti et al., 2017) suggest the traced cells might represent only a fraction of the complete presynaptic population, rendering smaller, more distributed projections more difficult to identify.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Albisetti et al., 2017 regarding transmission biases.

claim: Background contamination of native-coat particles in pseudotyped stock can result in false identification of projecting populations.
source: Furthermore, since large quantities of native-coat particles are routinely used to initiate the pseudotyping step of the viral production protocol (Osakada and Callaway, 2013), background contamination of native-coat particles in the pseudotyped stock is nearly unavoidable, which can result in false identification of projecting populations directly labeled by native-coat particles and not transsynaptically through the starter cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Osakada and Callaway, 2013 regarding the production protocol, and represents a logical inference about the consequences of contamination.

claim: CVS-N2c rabies strain identifies 5-20 fold more presynaptic cells per starter cell than SAD B19.
source: Recently, the deployment of the highly neurotropic CVS-N2c rabies strain for monosynaptic tracing was shown to identify 5–20 fold more presynaptic cells per starter cell than SAD B19, enabling a more comprehensive analysis of the diversity of presynaptic cells innervating a predesignated starter population.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Reardon et al., 2016, the original paper describing CVS-N2c vectors.

claim: CVS-N2c strain is less neurotoxic than SAD B19, making it more suitable for experiments in behaving animals.
source: In addition, this strain was shown to be less neurotoxic, making it more suitable for experiments in behaving animals.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Reardon et al., 2016.

claim: The production process for CVS-N2c vectors is time-consuming and yields low viral titers.
source: However, the production process for these vectors is time-consuming and yields low viral titers (Reardon et al., 2016), presumably due to the use of neuronal cell lines for the various amplification and packaging steps.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Reardon et al., 2016 and represents inference about the cause (neuronal cell lines).

claim: Low titers of CVS-N2c vectors have restricted more widespread use of the superior CVS-N2c vector in circuit mapping experiments.
source: This limitation has so far restricted more widespread use of the superior CVS-N2c vector in circuit mapping experiments, particularly in its more useful pseudotyped form, whose preparation is even lengthier and the titers lower still.
evidence: This represents an inference about the impact of production limitations on adoption of the technology.

claim: HEK293-GT cells stably express chimeric SAD B19 codon optimized glycoprotein (oG) and optimized T7 RNA polymerase (oT7pol).
source: (1) "HEK293-GT" cells, based on HEK293T cells stably expressing the chimeric SAD B19 codon optimized glycoprotein (oG) comprised of the extracellular domain of the Pasteur strain G and the transmembrane domain of the SAD B19G, along with the optimized T7 RNA polymerase (oT7pol), used for the initial rescue and amplification of native-coat particles
evidence: This is directly stated in the description of the new cell lines and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: BHK-eT cells stably express envA glycoprotein and TVA receptor.
source: (2) 'BHK-eT' cells, based on BHK21 cells stably expressing the envA glycoprotein, along with the TVA receptor, used for simultaneous vector pseudotyping and amplification (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is directly stated in the description of the new cell lines and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The chimeric oG can efficiently rescue both SAD B19 and CVS-N2c strains.
source: The oG was selected for use in the rescue cell line because it can be used to efficiently rescue both the SAD B19 and the CVS-N2c strains and effectively transduce all cell types, whereas particles coated with the N2cG are highly specific to neuronal cell types and do not effectively transduce HEK293 or BHK-21 cells.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the design choice and is supported by the successful rescue of both strains shown in the results.

claim: Particles coated with N2cG are highly specific to neuronal cell types and do not effectively transduce HEK293 or BHK-21 cells.
source: The oG was selected for use in the rescue cell line because it can be used to efficiently rescue both the SAD B19 and the CVS-N2c strains and effectively transduce all cell types, whereas particles coated with the N2cG are highly specific to neuronal cell types and do not effectively transduce HEK293 or BHK-21 cells.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the design choice and represents knowledge about the properties of N2cG.

claim: Both HEK-GT and BHK-eT cell lines use antibiotic resistance genes and strong constitutive promoters to improve selection.
source: To improve the selection process for the transgene carrying cells, both cell lines make use of antibiotic resistance genes and strong constitutive promoters (Norrman et al., 2018).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by citation to Norrman et al., 2018 regarding the use of strong promoters.

claim: The use of antibiotic resistance genes and strong constitutive promoters ensures that cultures consist of purely transgene-expressing cells with high expression levels.
source: This ensures that cultures consist of purely transgene-expressing cells and that expression levels in those cells are high (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C showing removal of non-expressing cells.

claim: Co-expression of TVA and envA in BHK-eT cells allows pseudotyped particles to propagate within the culture.
source: Furthermore, unlike previous packaging systems, the co-expression of TVA and envA in the BHK-eT cell line allows pseudotyped particles to propagate within the culture, similar to the native-coat ones (Figure 1F and G), enabling amplification and pseudotyping of vectors in a single short step.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by data in Figure 1F and G showing time course of amplification.

claim: A very small amount of native-coat or trace amounts of pseudotyped virus are sufficient to initiate the pseudotyping process in BHK-eT cells.
source: In addition, since a very small amount of native-coat, or even trace amounts of pseudotyped virus, are sufficient in order to initiate the pseudotyping process, contamination from native-coat particles in the final pseudotyped stock can be minimized, while the titer of the pseudotyped stock can be exceedingly high (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by data in Figure 1H showing high titers achieved.

claim: For each new viral batch produced (37 in total), injection of pseudotyped particles at work concentrations into naïve brains resulted in only minimal non-specific labeling (maximum of 1-2 labeled cells per 0.5-1 mm of tissue).
source: For each new viral batch produced (37 in total), we injected pseudotyped particles at work concentrations (1–5×108 TU ml-1) into naïve brains. We found only minimal non-specific labeling (a maximum of 1–2 labelled cells per 0.5–1 mm of tissue examined).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result from testing 37 viral batches.

claim: Sparse non-specific labeling of pseudotyped particles can occur in the absence of TVA when extremely high vector titers (100-500-fold higher than experimental requirements) are introduced into the brain.
source: Even though the presence of native coat particles can be virtually eliminated from the preparation, it is still possible to see sparse non-specific labeling of pseudotyped particles in the absence of TVA, when extremely high vector titers (100–500-fold higher to our experimental requirements) are introduced into the brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Non-specific labeling from envA-pseudotyped particles results from direct penetration into damaged cells and cell processes along the needle tract rather than from native coat particles.
source: To demonstrate that even this sparse labeling likely results from direct penetration of pseudotyped particles into damaged cells and cell processes along the needle tract, rather than from non-specific labeling with native coat particles, we transduced organotypic hippocampal cultures prepared from a WT mouse brain with envA-pseudotyped CVS-N2c-tdTomato, either immediately or one hour after lacerating the culture with a scalpel, to simulate physical damage to neuronal processes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C-E showing higher transduction immediately after tissue damage.

claim: Cultures transduced immediately after physical insult exhibited substantially higher transduction rates than cultures transduced one hour later.
source: We observed that cultures transduced immediately after the insult exhibited substantially higher transduction rates than cultures transduced one hour later, after most damaged processes had time to recover (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E)
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental observation and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: Physical damage accompanying intracerebral injection can produce off-target labeling around the injection site when high-titer virus is delivered.
source: confirming that physical damage (such as one that accompanies intracerebral injection with a Hamilton needle), can produce off-target labeling around the injection site, when high-titer virus is delivered.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the organotypic culture experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: oG coated CVS-N2c particles produced in HEK293-GT cells can be successfully used for non-specific retrograde labeling.
source: Furthermore, beyond their use as an intermediate to obtain envA-pseudotyped particles, we confirmed that oG coated CVS-N2c particles produced in HEK293-GT cells can be successfully used for non-specific retrograde labeling (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B showing retrograde labeling from hippocampus.

claim: The new cell lines enable significantly faster production times, higher titers and less background contamination than both other currently used methods for production of either CVS-N2c or SAD B19.
source: Together, these new cell lines enable significantly faster production times, higher titers and less background contamination than both other currently used methods for production of either CVS-N2c or SAD B19 (Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by comparative data in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: Delivery of AAV-DIO-EF1a-TVA-2A-N2cG into dentate gyrus of Prox1cre mice followed by RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-EGFP resulted in exclusive transduction of FLAG3X-tagged dentate granule cells.
source: To test the efficacy and transduction exclusivity of these new vectors, we first delivered a minimal volume (20 nl) of AAV vectors expressing a cre-dependent TVA(FLAG3X)–2A-N2cG cassette into the dentate gyrus (DG) of a Prox1cre mouse (Borges-Merjane et al., 2020) followed by large volume (500 nl) of RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-EGFP vectors into the same location. Subsequent immunolabeling revealed that only dentate granule cells (DGCs) immunoreactive for the FLAG3X tag were transduced by the rabies vectors, with efficient retrograde labeling from this small group to neurons in the entorhinal cortex (EC, Figure 2A; Borges-Merjane et al., 2020).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Retrograde labeling from adult-born DGCs using Ascl1creERT2 × Ai14 mice resulted in widespread and specific labeling of layer-2 neurons of MEC and LEC, hilar mossy cells, CA3 pyramidal cells, and DG-projecting subcortical regions.
source: This manipulation resulted in both highly specific targeting of tdTomato+ adult-born DGCs in the inner granule cell layer, as well as robust retrograde labeling of afferents to these starter cells. This high efficacy manifested as widespread and specific labeling of layer-2 neurons of the medial and lateral entorhinal cortices (MEC and LEC, respectively), hilar mossy cells, CA3 pyramidal cells and a number of DG-projecting subcortical regions, including the medial septal (MS), the supramamilary (SuM), and the raphe (RN) nuclei (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B), largely consistent with several previous reports (Deshpande et al., 2013; Vivar et al., 2012).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B, with citations to previous reports.

claim: Expression of cre-dependent TVA-2A-tdTomato without rabies glycoprotein in DGCs followed by high-volume, high-titer RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-EGFP resulted in exclusive EGFP expression in tdTomato-positive neurons with no retrograde labeling.
source: Last, to ensure that the envA pseudotyped virus produced using our system lacks non-specific targeting properties and cannot propagate in the absence of its glycoprotein, we expressed a cre-dependent TVA-2A-tdTomato cassette, without the rabies glycoprotein, in DGCs, again using Prox1cre mice. Subsequent delivery of high-volume (0.5 µl), high-titer (~3 × 1010 TU ml–1) RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-EGFP vectors resulted in exclusive expression of EGFP in dTomato-positive neurons in the DG (Figure 2C) but not in dTomato-negative regions, or in any of the regions projecting to the DG.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The new packaging system is capable of rapidly producing high-titer and high-quality RVdGenvA vectors for transsynaptic retrograde neuronal labeling.
source: These experiments provide evidence that the new packaging system we designed is capable of rapidly producing high-titer and high-quality RVdGenvA vectors for transsynaptic retrograde neuronal labeling.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: CVS-N2c vectors were originally produced in N2A cells under the premise that this would improve neurotropism and reduce neurotoxicity.
source: RVdG-CVS-N2c vectors were originally produced in the neural progenitor cell line N2A, under the premise that this would improve neurotropism of the assembled viruses, enhancing their trans-synaptic transfer rates and reducing their neurotoxicity (Reardon et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Reardon et al., 2016.

claim: Comparison of CVS-N2c vectors produced in N2A versus BHK-eT cells showed highly efficient and specific retrograde labeling of CA1 afferents in equal proportions for both vectors.
source: To evaluate any differences in retrograde labeling efficiency between the vectors assembled using the two approaches, we expressed a TVA-2A-N2cG cassette in CA1 pyramidal neurons and subsequently transduced them with a cocktail of two different RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c vectors expressing either EGFP or dTomato, in equal titers, amplified and pseudotyped using either N2A-based or the new HEK-GT/BHK-eT based packaging systems (Figure 3A). This strategy resulted in highly efficient and specific retrograde labeling of CA1 afferents in the CA3, LEC and medial septum (MS) in equal proportions for both vectors (Figure 3B, C and H).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 3B, C and H.

claim: CVS-N2c vectors produced in BHK-eT cells visibly outnumbered SAD B19 vectors in labeling CA1 afferents in most regions tested.
source: To confirm that these CVS-N2c vectors remain more efficient than the widely used SAD B19 strain, as was previously shown for vectors produced in N2A cells (Reardon et al., 2016; Rowland et al., 2013), the previous experimental design was repeated, using the optimized B19 glycoprotein (oG; Kim et al., 2016) and RVdGenvA-SAD B19 vectors (Figure 3D). Here, a strikingly different result was observed, with afferents labeled with CVS-N2c visibly outnumbering those labeled with SAD B19 in most regions tested (Figure 3E, F and H).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental observation and shown in Figure 3E, F and H.

claim: The ratio of 2nd order neurons between CVS-N2c and SAD B19 differed substantially, with differences close to an order of magnitude in most regions except MS.
source: Quantification of cell numbers in these experiments showed that while the ratio of 1st order CA1 neurons between the two compared vectors remained low in both experiments (Figure 3G), the ratios of 2nd order neurons in the tested sets of regions differed substantially, with only minor differences observed when the two CVS-N2c vectors were compared, but differences close to an order of magnitude observed when CVS-N2c and SAD B19 vectors were compared (Ipsilateral CA3: 14.43 ± 1.67%; Contralateral CA3: 11.95 ± 2.85%; LEC: 8.17 ± 0.85%; MS: 100.88 ± 4.54%; Figure 3H). A notable exception is seen in the projection from the MS, in which ratios between the SAD B19 and N2c remained identical.
evidence: This is directly stated with quantitative data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: CVS-N2c vectors propagate less efficiently when using oG as opposed to their endogenous N2cG.
source: Since we observed that CVS-N2c vectors propagate less efficiently when using the oG, as opposed to their endogenous N2cG (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C), the actual differences in retrograde labeling between CVS-N2c and SAD B19 are likely to be substantially higher, matching those previously reported (Reardon et al., 2016).
evidence: This is directly stated as an observation and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Retrograde labeling from DG in Prox1cre × GAD1-EGFP mice revealed neurons in S.O. and S.LM. but not in S.P. or S.R. layers.
source: To test if we could locate and identify these cells, we targeted RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-tdTomato vectors to DGCs of Prox1cre mice crossed with GAD1-EGFP transgenic mice, in which GABAergic neurons are fluorescently labeled (Tamamaki et al., 2003), and examined the regions outside of the DG for colocalization (Figure 4A). Consistent with these reports, we found extensive labeling of neurons with N2c-tdTomato, whose somata were located in the S.O. and S.LM., but not in the Stratum Pyramidal (S.P.) or Radiatum (S.R.) layers.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 4A and B, with citation to Tamamaki et al., 2003.

claim: A third population of DG-projecting neurons was uncovered in the superficial most layer of the subiculum.
source: In addition, we uncovered a third population of DG-projecting neurons in the superficial most layer of the subiculum (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is directly stated as a novel finding and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Half of all retrogradely labeled neurons in S.O. and S.LM. were positive for EGFP (GAD1), while in the subicular population colocalization was almost completely absent.
source: Analysis of colocalization has revealed that while half of all retrogradely labeled neurons found in the S.O and S.LM. were also positive for EGFP, in the subicular population, which accounted for more than a third of all intrahippocampal projecting cells, colocalization was almost completely absent (Figure 4C), suggesting that this population consists of excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The subicular population projecting to DG likely consists of excitatory neurons.
source: in the subicular population, which accounted for more than a third of all intrahippocampal projecting cells, colocalization was almost completely absent (Figure 4C), suggesting that this population consists of excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the lack of GAD1 colocalization, and further supported by AAV experiments in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: AAV-mDLX-EGFP injection into CA1 revealed axonal arborizations in the molecular layer of the DG.
source: AAV vectors expressing EGFP under control of either the inhibitory neuron-specific mDLX or the excitatory neuron-specific CaMKIIa promoters, injected into the superficial CA1 or superficial subiculum, respectively, confirmed the existence of axonal branching in the DG (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: AAV-CaMKII-EGFP injection into subiculum revealed axonal arborizations in the molecular layer of the DG.
source: AAV vectors expressing EGFP under control of either the inhibitory neuron-specific mDLX or the excitatory neuron-specific CaMKIIa promoters, injected into the superficial CA1 or superficial subiculum, respectively, confirmed the existence of axonal branching in the DG (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is directly stated and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 43 ± 5% of S.O. retrogradely-labeled neurons were positive for Sst.
source: Taking advantage of the high-throughput nature of our labeling approach, we immunostained sections from labeled animals for two of the most prominent interneuron markers, Parvalbumin (Pvalb) and Somatostatin (Sst), and found that while 43 ± 5% of S.O. retrogradely-labeled neurons were positive for Sst, none of the labeled cells in both S.O. and S.LM colocalized with Pvalb (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is directly stated as a quantitative result and shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: None of the retrogradely-labeled cells in S.O. and S.LM. colocalized with Pvalb.
source: we immunostained sections from labeled animals for two of the most prominent interneuron markers, Parvalbumin (Pvalb) and Somatostatin (Sst), and found that while 43 ± 5% of S.O. retrogradely-labeled neurons were positive for Sst, none of the labeled cells in both S.O. and S.LM colocalized with Pvalb (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: The lack of Pvalb colocalization is consistent with the known projection pattern of S.O. Sst neurons to S.LM. and the projection pattern of Pvalb neurons mainly to pyramidal cell layer.
source: This is consistent with the known projection of S.O. Sst neurons to the S.LM., which borders on the dentate gyrus, while axons of Pvalb neurons in the CA1 project mainly to the pyramidal cell layer and have few, if any axonal arborization in the S.LM. (Freund and Buzsáki, 1996) and are therefore much less likely to branch into the DG.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation consistent with known anatomy, supported by citation to Freund and Buzsáki, 1996.

claim: AAV vectors with cre-off mechanism using SEO can drive transgene expression under control of CaMKIIa promoter.
source: First, we wanted to be able to compare between two genetically distinct, yet spatially overlapping populations. To this aim, we designed AAV vectors which contain a cre-off mechanism, using a single-floxed, excisable open reading frame (SEO) to drive transgene expression under control of the excitatory neuronal CaMKIIa promoter (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is directly stated and illustrated in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In Calb1cre mice, Cre recombinase is expressed exclusively in deep, but not in superficial CA1 neurons.
source: We tested this tool on CA1 pyramidal neurons of Calb1cre mice, in which Cre recombinase is expressed exclusively in deep, but not in superficial CA1 neurons (Li et al., 2017; Valero et al., 2015; Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Li et al., 2017 and Valero et al., 2015, and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Parallel retrograde labeling from superficial and deep CA1 neurons revealed that both receive relatively equal input from CA3 neurons, but deep CA1 neurons receive substantially greater input from LEC-3 neurons.
source: Parallel retrograde labeling from these two subpopulations of CA1 neurons revealed that while both receive relatively equal input from CA3 neurons, deep CA1 neurons receive substantially greater input from LEC-3 neurons (Figure 5B), confirming previous findings obtained using lower-throughput approaches (Li et al., 2017; Masurkar et al., 2017).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result shown in Figure 5B, with citations to previous reports.

claim: Retrograde labeling from hippocampal inhibitory neurons using AAV-mDLX-TVA-2A-N2cG in GAD1-EGFP mice revealed widespread labeling in CA1, CA3, and EC.
source: To attain interneuron-specific retrograde labeling, we first used AAV vectors to express the TVA-2A-N2cG cassette under control of the interneuron-specific mDLX promoter (Dimidschstein et al., 2013) in the CA1 of GAD1-EGFP mice. A subsequent injection of CVS-N2c-tdTomato revealed widespread labeling of 2nd order neurons both within the hippocampal CA1 and CA3 fields, as well as in the EC (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, with citation to Dimidschstein et al., 2013.

claim: A small population of long-range inhibitory projection neurons to hippocampal interneurons is located preferentially in EC layers 5a and 6.
source: An additional analysis of co-labeling in the EC revealed a small population of long-range inhibitory projection neurons, located preferentially in the deeper layers 5 a and 6 (Figure 5D), whose existence has previously been reported (Basu et al., 2016; Melzer et al., 2012) but their location within the EC has so far remained unknown.
evidence: This is directly stated as a novel finding regarding location, with citations to previous reports of existence, and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Using Dlx5/6flpE × Ai65 mice with flp-dependent TVA-2A-N2cG and RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-EGFP-iCre, inhibitory projections to hippocampal inhibitory neurons can be isolated.
source: In order to cross-validate and expand on these findings, we crossed Dlx5/6flpE mice with the double cre +flp, tdTomato reporter line Ai65 (Madisen et al., 2015). Hereby, using injections of AAV vectors with flp-dependent TVA-2A-N2cG expression cassette, followed by RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-EGFP-iCre, we were able to highlight and isolate the inhibitory projections to hippocampal inhibitory neurons, as the double cre +flp recombination required for tdTomato expression can only take place in inhibitory neurons transduced by the rabies virus (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental approach and shown in Figure 5E, with citation to Madisen et al., 2015.

claim: While the majority of excitatory cortical input to hippocampal inhibitory neurons originated in superficial layers 2 and 3, long-range inhibitory projection neurons are almost exclusively found in deeper layers 5a and 6.
source: In line with our previous findings, we show that while the majority of excitatory cortical input to hippocampal inhibitory neurons originated in the superficial layers 2 and 3, long-range inhibitory projection neurons are almost exclusively found in the deeper layers 5 a and 6 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: In the MS and DBB, a large fraction of cells projecting to hippocampal inhibitory neurons are double-labeled (inhibitory).
source: Further examination of labeling patterns of 2nd order neurons in deep-brain regions showed that in the MS and the diagonal band of Broca (DBB), a large fraction of cells are double-labeled, confirming that our labeling strategy for isolation of long-range inhibitory projections is exhaustive (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The deeper cortical layers give rise to both inhibitory and excitatory hippocampal projections, with the excitatory projection originating from a substantially larger population.
source: This strongly suggests that while the deeper cortical layers give rise to both inhibitory and excitatory hippocampal projections, the excitatory projection originated from a substantially larger population.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: Only sporadic evidence existed for the presence of cortico-hippocampal projections arising from the deeper layers of the EC.
source: This is particularly unexpected, as to-date, only sporadic evidence existed for the presence of cortico-hippocampal projections, excitatory or inhibitory, arising from the deeper layers of the EC (Gloveli et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Gloveli et al., 2001.

claim: The B19 N-P linker sequence can be used for separation of exogenous genes in rabies vectors.
source: A previous report has shown that the B19 N-P linker sequence, which allows the virus to effectively separate these proteins, can also be used for separation of exogenous genes (Osakada et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Osakada et al., 2018.

claim: Bicistronic CVS-N2c vectors using the N-P linker efficiently express individual proteins in a compartment-specific manner.
source: To test the feasibility and efficacy of this approach, we designed new CVS-N2c bicistronic plasmids, to drive co-expression of a nuclear-localized EGFP (nl.EGFP) with either tdTomato (Figure 6A) or a synaptophysin-tethered EGFP for specific labeling of presynaptic terminals (SypEGFP, Figure 6B) separated by the CVS-N2c N-P liker sequence. Specific delivery of these vectors to hippocampal DGCs using targeted AAV expression of the cre-dependent TVA-2A-N2cG cassette in Prox1cre mice, revealed that in both cases, the individual proteins were efficiently expressed in a compartment-specific manner (Figure 6A and B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-D).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 6A and B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: Bicistronic CVS-N2c vectors expressing tdTomato and oChIEF enable reliable optogenetic activation of labeled neurons at high frequencies.
source: Next, we capitalized on this result to create new bicistronic vectors for dual expression of the optogenetic actuator ChIEF (Lin et al., 2009), along with a fluorescent protein, speculating that the increased expression levels and the untethering of the fluorophore will lead to greater responsivity of labeled neurons to optogenetic stimulation, as well as facilitate their identification. We again targeted DGCs for retrograde labeling using these new vectors and recorded the action potential success rate of labeled neurons in the EC, following five light pulses, each 1 ms long, at varying frequencies. As predicted, action potentials could be reliably generated at much higher stimulation frequencies and at a much earlier time point following stimulation onset than has previously been shown for both SAD B19 and CVS-N2c vectors (Osakada et al., 2018; Reardon et al., 2016: Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 6C and D, with citations to previous reports.

claim: In recorded neurons labeled with CVS-N2c-tdTomato-oChIEF, the resting membrane potential was −55 mV to −75 mV, corroborating functional integrity.
source: In these recorded neurons, the resting membrane potential was −55 mV to −75 mV, corroborating the functional integrity of the cells.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental observation shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Bicistronic CVS-N2c-tdTomato-oChIEF vectors can be reliably used for exploring circuit motifs by recording synaptic responses to optogenetic stimulation.
source: By recording synaptic responses to optogenetic stimulation from several neuronal populations sharing the same input as DGCs, such as neighboring, non-transduced DGCs, CA3 pyramidal neurons and dentate gyrus molecular layer interneurons, we also show that this tool can be reliably used for exploring circuit motifs, and also potentially for effective circuit-based manipulation in behaving animals (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Under in vitro conditions, cellular health and viability begin to deteriorate in preparations made >10 days from RVdG-CVS-N2c injection.
source: Since our observations indicate that under in vitro conditions, cellular health and viability begin to deteriorate in preparations made >10 days from RVdG-CVS-N2c injection, it is important to show that effective optogenetic activation can be achieved at an earlier time point, when the cells remain healthy and viable for the duration of the experiment.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiments.

claim: RVdG-CVS-N2c vectors have been shown to be less neurotoxic than SAD B19 strain and compatible for prolonged imaging of neuronal activity in vivo.
source: RVdG-CVS-N2c vectors have previously been shown to be less neurotoxic than the SAD B19 strain, and compatible for prolonged imaging of neuronal activity in vivo (Reardon et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Reardon et al., 2016.

claim: First GCaMP8m labeled neurons were detected at day 3 after RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-GCaMP8m injection in V1.
source: In the following weeks, we observed the time course of GCaMP8m expression and recorded calcium transients of the labeled 1st and 2nd order neurons using two-photon imaging, in response to visual cues in three awake behaving mice. While we detected the first GCaMP8m labeled neurons already at day 3, substantial labeling at approximately half-maximal numbers in all animals started 7 days after RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-GCaMP8m injection.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental observation and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Substantial GCaMP8m labeling at approximately half-maximal numbers started 7 days after RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-GCaMP8m injection.
source: While we detected the first GCaMP8m labeled neurons already at day 3, substantial labeling at approximately half-maximal numbers in all animals started 7 days after RVdGenvA-CVS-N2c-GCaMP8m injection.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental observation and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The increase of GCaMP8m-labeled neuron numbers slowed and remained high until day 16 (on average 1100 neurons).
source: Subsequently, the increase of neuronal numbers slowed and remained high until day 16 (on average 1100 neurons), when the experiments were terminated (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental observation and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Both tdTomato-positive (putative 1st order) and tdTomato-negative 2nd order neurons showed similar tuning properties to visual stimuli.
source: Each session, we recorded fluorescence time series for a subset of the GCaMP8m-labeled neurons and determined their calcium activity while presenting drifting grating stimuli to the mouse in a visual dome setup (Figure 7D). Both tdTomato-positive (putative 1st order) neurons as well as tdTomato-negative 2nd order neurons showed similar tuning properties (Figure 7E and F) with preferred directions slightly biased in the horizontal plane (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 7D-G.

claim: The fluorescence signal-to-noise ratio per neuron and the proportion of direction tuned neurons remained constant from day 7 to day 16.
source: The fluorescence signal-to-noise ratio per neuron (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C) and the proportion of direction tuned neurons (Figure 7H) remained constant from day 7 to the conclusion of the experiments at day 16.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result and shown in Figure 7H and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: RVdG-CVS-N2c viral vectors can be reliably used for in vivo experiments in behaving animals for circuit-specific recording and manipulation of activity from day 7 to day 16.
source: These experiments demonstrate that RVdG-CVS-N2c viral vectors can be reliably used for in vivo experiments in behaving animals for circuit-specific recording and manipulation of activity and delineate a time period during which the neurons retain their normal physiological properties.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the in vivo imaging experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: The increased labeling efficiency of CVS-N2c stems from the N2c strain itself, rather than its production process in N2A cells.
source: As this premise has not been directly tested, we surmised that the increased labeling efficiency stems from the N2c strain itself, rather than its production process, and created an alternative packaging system to optimize all the different steps of production.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis that was tested, and the results in Figure 3 support this conclusion.

claim: The co-expression of TVA and envA in pseudotyping cell lines reduces to a minimum the amount of native-coat virus needed to initiate the process.
source: The additional co-expression of TVA and envA in the pseudotyping cell lines reduces to a minimum the amount of native-coat virus needed to initiate the process, thereby nearly abolishing the presence of these particles in the pseudotyped stock, and vastly increasing tracing specificity.
evidence: This is directly stated as a design feature and its consequences, supported by data showing minimal background contamination.

claim: The advantage of minimal native-coat contamination is particularly relevant when performing retrograde labeling from single cells.
source: This advantage is particularly relevant when performing retrograde labeling from single cells (Rossi et al., 2020; Wertz et al., 2015; Wickersham et al., 2007b) where a small number of non-specifically labeled neurons can potentially account for a large fraction of the entire labeled population.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about the importance of the improvement, with citations to single-cell tracing papers.

claim: Vectors produced using the HEK-GT/BHKeT packaging system show comparable retrograde labeling efficiency to ones produced in N2A cells.
source: We show that contrary to the premise, vectors produced using the HEK-GT/BHKeT packaging system show comparable retrograde labeling efficiency to ones produced in N2A cells and significantly higher than that of SAD B19 particles.
evidence: This is directly stated as a conclusion and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Vectors produced using the HEK-GT/BHKeT packaging system show significantly higher retrograde labeling efficiency than SAD B19 particles.
source: We show that contrary to the premise, vectors produced using the HEK-GT/BHKeT packaging system show comparable retrograde labeling efficiency to ones produced in N2A cells and significantly higher than that of SAD B19 particles.
evidence: This is directly stated as a conclusion and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Neurons transduced with CVS-N2c vectors produced using the new cell lines maintain viability and physiological function for at least 16 days.
source: While we show that neurons transduced with CVS-N2c vectors produced using our cell lines maintain viability and physiological function for at least 16 days, since no direct comparisons of physiological properties and long-term viability were made with vectors produced in the N2A line, it remains possible that packaging these vectors in N2A cells would result in reduced neurotoxicity, when compared with vector packaged in non-neuronal cell lines.
evidence: This is directly stated as an experimental result from the in vivo imaging experiments in Figure 7.

claim: It remains possible that packaging CVS-N2c vectors in N2A cells would result in reduced neurotoxicity compared with vectors packaged in non-neuronal cell lines.
source: While we show that neurons transduced with CVS-N2c vectors produced using our cell lines maintain viability and physiological function for at least 16 days, since no direct comparisons of physiological properties and long-term viability were made with vectors produced in the N2A line, it remains possible that packaging these vectors in N2A cells would result in reduced neurotoxicity, when compared with vector packaged in non-neuronal cell lines.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about a possibility that was not directly tested.

claim: The subicular neurons projecting to DG have pyramidal-like morphology and spiny dendritic arbors.
source: Since in the GAD1-EGFP line not all inhibitory neurons may express the fluorescent marker (Tamamaki et al., 2003), it remains a possibility that these neurons are also inhibitory but are somehow genetically indisposed to express the marker. However, their pyramidal-like morphology, spiny dendritic arbors and putative expression of the CaMKIIa promoter, all hallmarks of excitatory neurons, render this possibility unlikely.
evidence: This is inferred from the statement that these features are hallmarks of excitatory neurons, and can be observed in the images in Figure 4.

claim: The subicular neurons projecting to DG putatively express the CaMKIIa promoter.
source: However, their pyramidal-like morphology, spiny dendritic arbors and putative expression of the CaMKIIa promoter, all hallmarks of excitatory neurons, render this possibility unlikely.
evidence: This is stated as putative expression, supported by AAV-CaMKII-EGFP experiments in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The CVS-N2c endogenous N-P linker can effectively separate at least two individual elements, and possibly more.
source: Here, we adapted this approach for CVS-N2c vectors by inserting the virus's endogenous N-P linker between two coding sequences, which led to efficient separation of the proteins with no observable effect on the expression levels of either.
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by data in Figure 6A and B showing separation of two proteins, with speculation about more.

claim: The separation of fluorophore from optogenetic actuators can increase their light responsiveness due to improved membrane trafficking and higher expression levels.
source: Apart from enabling better tracking of distinct subcellular compartments, we also show that the separation of the fluorophore from optogenetic actuators can increase their light responsiveness, possibly as a result of improved membrane trafficking and higher expression levels.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Some of the improved optogenetic properties should be attributed to the improved ChR2 variant (ChIEF) used.
source: However, some of these properties should also be attributed to the improved ChR2 variant we used, which was shown to possess faster kinetics (Lin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citation to Lin et al., 2009 describing ChIEF properties.

claim: The untethering of the fluorophore from membrane-bound proteins leads to its predominantly cytosolic expression, facilitating better identification of labeled neurons.
source: Another benefit of this separation is better identification of labeled neurons, since the untethering of the fluorophore from membrane-bound proteins leads to its predominantly cytosolic expression.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and benefit of the bicistronic design.

claim: The new packaging system enables a fast, simple and highly effective approach for circuit mapping in the mammalian brain.
source: Together, this system enables a fast, simple and highly effective approach for circuit mapping in the mammalian brain.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion summarizing the overall contribution of the work.
